title: Proper direct image gives a compactifiable comparison
statement: Use the finite coefficients and schemes of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Let $c:C\to X\times_kX$ and $b:B\to Y\times_kY$ be correspondences of separated finite-type $k$-schemes, and let $p:X\to Y$, $q:C\to B$ be proper with $b_iq=pc_i$ for $i=1,2$, a proper diagram as in [def-trf-coefficient-pushforward]. Let $p_Z:Z\to\bar Z$ be its induced maps on the fixed diagrams of [def-trf-cohomological-comparison], including $p_s=\operatorname{id}_s$ and $p_F:\operatorname{Fix}(c)\to\operatorname{Fix}(b)$ of [lem-trf-fixed-map-proper]. Use the admissible constructible adjunctions of [def-trf-admissibility]. Then $f_Z=Rp_{Z*}=Rp_{Z!}$ with its usual lax tensor map, ordinary exchange $\bar g^*Rp_{V*}\to Rp_{U*}g^*$, exceptional exchange $Rp_{U!}g^!\to\bar g^!Rp_{V!}$ and $\iota=\operatorname{id}_A$ is a compactifiable pre-comparison satisfying all seven requirements of [def-trf-cohomological-comparison]. The mates are the canonical direct-image and compact-support composition maps for $\bar g p_U=p_Vg$. The evaluation-defined duality comparison is the proper adjunction isomorphism $Rp_{Z*}D_ZM\cong D_{\bar Z}Rp_{Z*}M$ with its trace counit. All assertions use the specified adjunction maps, without a Cartesian assumption on the leg squares or properness of $X,Y,C,B$ over $k$.

source.place: §4.1.4(a), proper push-forward, including its compactification argument

proof.text: Fix the finite coefficient stage and the proper correspondence diagram from [def-trf-coefficient-conventions] and [def-trf-coefficient-pushforward]. The relations $b_iq=pc_i$ induce the maps $p_X=p$, $p_{X\times X}=p\times p$, $p_C=q$, $p_F=h$, and $p_s=\operatorname{id}_s$ on every labelled fixed-diagram object. The factorization and properness assertion of [lem-trf-fixed-map-proper] makes $p_F$ proper; $p$, $q$, and $p\times p$ are proper by the hypotheses and the same fixed-map lemma, and the identity is proper. Thus every $p_Z$ is proper. On the finite-Tor constructible domains supplied by [def-trf-admissibility], set $f_Z=Rp_{Z*}=Rp_{Z!}$, using the proper identification in [prop-functor-package]. For each labelled arrow $g:U\to V$, the equality $p_Vg=\bar g p_U$ gives the ordinary exchange $\alpha_g$ by the unit/counit mate, and the exceptional exchange $\beta_g$ by the specified exceptional adjunction. Their mates are therefore the direct-image and compact-support composition maps for this equality, by the mate definitions in [def-trf-cohomological-comparison]. Set $\iota=\operatorname{id}_A$. No leg square is required to be Cartesian.

source.place: §4.1.4(a), first paragraph: proper maps on each diagram object and the induced pre-morphism

proof.text: For each $Z$, take the lax tensor map $t_Z$ to be the adjoint of the composite $p_Z^*(Rp_{Z*}M\otimes Rp_{Z*}N)\cong p_Z^*Rp_{Z*}M\otimes p_Z^*Rp_{Z*}N\to M\otimes N$, the multiplication formula of [def-trf-kernel-pushforward-maps] applied to $p_Z$. Naturality of the counits, the associativity and signed symmetry of the derived tensor from [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], and the triangle identities in [def-trf-admissibility] show that transposing twice gives the same map, so $t_Z$ is commutative and associative. At $s$, $p_s=\operatorname{id}_s$ and the same unit/counit calculation gives $\iota\circ t_s=\iota\otimes\iota$ (with the unit identifications). These are exactly requirements (I) and (II) of [def-trf-cohomological-comparison].

source.place: §4.1.4(a), assertion that (I)–(IV) follow by adjointness; Definitions 4.1.1(c) and 4.1.3(I),(II)

proof.text: For composable labelled arrows $g:U\to V$ and $h:V\to W$, the equations $p_Vg=\bar g p_U$ and $p_Wh=\bar h p_V$ identify both composites with $p_Whg$. Proper direct-image composition, compact-support composition, and their identity and associativity equations are supplied by [prop-functor-package], with $Rf_!=Rf_*$ for the proper maps. The mate definition of $\alpha$ therefore gives $\alpha_{\operatorname{id}}=\operatorname{id}$ and $\alpha_{hg}=(\alpha_g h^*)\circ(\bar g^*\alpha_h)$, with the canonical pullback compositors. For tensor compatibility, transpose both sides along $p_U^*\dashv Rp_{U*}$: each is the two counits followed by the same tensor map, and naturality identifies the composites. Thus (III) and (IV) hold. The construction uses only the specified ordinary and exceptional adjunction maps, so it remains valid for non-Cartesian leg squares.

Fix a diagram object $Z$, write $p=p_Z$, $a=a_Z$ and $\bar a=a_{\bar Z}$, so $a=\bar ap$. The definition [def-trf-cohomological-comparison] gives $\delta_Z=\beta_a$, since $\iota=1$. Its exceptional transpose is $R\bar a_!Rp_!a^!A_s\cong Ra_!a^!A_s\to A_s$. By the composite-counit equation [fix-prop-adjunctions](3), and the conjugate composition identification of [def-trf-admissibility], this is precisely the transpose of the counit $Rp_!p^!\omega_{\bar Z}\to\omega_{\bar Z}$. Thus $\delta_Z=\tau_p$ of [def-trf-kernel-pushforward-maps]. As $t_Z=\mu_p$ by Step 2, the defining evaluation transpose of $d_Z$ is exactly that of $\chi_p$; hence $d_Z=\chi_p$.

source.place: §4.1.4(a), identification of the duality map with sheafified adjunction

proof.text:
We verify that this specific map is invertible, not merely that its endpoints are isomorphic. For $M\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,A)$, put $P=Rp_*M$. The internal adjunction [fix-lem-tensor-adjunction] with $N=\omega_{\bar Z}$ and $p^!N=\omega_Z$ gives an isomorphism $\lambda:Rp_*D_ZM\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{\bar Z}P$. Its Hom bijection is obtained by ordinary adjunction, tensor--Hom adjunction, exceptional adjunction and the projection isomorphism [prop-functor-package](5). Explicitly, $u:L\to Rp_*D_ZM$ corresponds to
$$L\otimes P\xrightarrow{\operatorname{PF}}Rp_*(p^*L\otimes M)\xrightarrow{Rp_*(\widetilde u\otimes1)}Rp_*(D_ZM\otimes M)\xrightarrow{Rp_*\mathrm{ev}}Rp_*\omega_Z\xrightarrow{\tau_p}\omega_{\bar Z},$$
where $\widetilde u=\varepsilon_p\circ p^*u$. Naturality of the projection map and the identity $\mu_{p,D_ZM,M}=Rp_*(1\otimes\varepsilon_p)\circ\operatorname{PF}$ of [lem-trf-dual-pushforward-evaluation-counit], with the signed symmetry inserted, identify this composite with $\tau_p\circ Rp_*\mathrm{ev}\circ\mu_p\circ(u\otimes1)$. The first identity of that lemma says this is $\mathrm{ev}_P\circ(\chi_pu\otimes1)$. Tensor--Hom adjunction therefore gives $\lambda u=\chi_pu$ for every $u$; taking $u=1$ gives $\lambda=\chi_p=d_Z$. This proves (V). The argument uses only the finite-Tor domains and the specified adjunctions.

source.place: §4.1.4(a), axiom (V): sheafified adjunction, with its evaluation transpose written out

proof.text: Let $g:U\to V$ and $\bar g:\bar U\to\bar V$ both be proper. By the mate definition in [def-trf-cohomological-comparison], $\alpha_{g,*}:Rp_{V*}Rg_*\to R\bar g_*Rp_{U*}$ is the transpose of $\bar g^*Rp_{V*}Rg_*\xrightarrow{\alpha_g}Rp_{U*}g^*Rg_*\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_g}Rp_{U*}$. Since $\alpha_g$ is itself the mate of the equality $p_Vg=\bar gp_U$ (Step 1), the composite-counit formula of [fix-prop-adjunctions] (3) and the triangle identities identify $\alpha_{g,*}$ with the ordinary composition comparison $Rp_{V*}Rg_*\cong R(p_Vg)_*=R(\bar gp_U)_*\cong R\bar g_*Rp_{U*}$, an isomorphism. In the same way $\beta_{g,!}$, transposed from $\beta_g$ with the exceptional unit of [def-trf-admissibility], is the compact-support composition comparison $R\bar g_!Rp_{U!}\cong R(\bar gp_U)_!=R(p_Vg)_!\cong Rp_{V!}Rg_!$ of [thm-sf-comp-composition], an isomorphism. Clause (1) of [lem-trf-compact-composition-proper-square-normalization], applied with $t=p_V$, $t_W=p_U$, $h=g$, $h'=\bar g$, says exactly that this compact-support comparison is the ordinary direct-image composition comparison under proper coincidence. Thus, under these identifications, $\beta_{g,!}$ is the composite of the two ordinary composition isomorphisms in the reverse direction, i.e. the inverse of $\alpha_{g,*}$. This is requirement (VI) of [def-trf-cohomological-comparison].

source.place: §4.1.4(a), assertion (VI): proper direct-image composition and adjointness

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-proper-diagram-compactification] to the two legs of $c,b$ and the proper maps $p,q$. It supplies proper compactifications of $X,Y,C,B$, extensions $c^*,b^*,p^*,q^*$ satisfying both leg equations, and Cartesian restriction squares on $X,Y$ and $C,B$. Products give the Cartesian square on $X\times_kX,Y\times_kY$. The induced fixed-scheme square is also Cartesian: a point of $\operatorname{Fix}(c^*)$ lying over $\operatorname{Fix}(b)$ has its $C^*$ coordinate in $C=q^{*-1}(B)$, and its $X^*$ coordinate lies in $X$ because its diagonal lies in $X\times X$. This argument is scheme-theoretic: substitute $C=C^*\times_{B^*}B$ and $X=X^*\times_{Y^*}Y$ in the defining fibre products of the fixed schemes [def-trf-coefficient-pushforward, def-trf-cohomological-comparison], and reassociate the fibre products. The square at $s$ is the identity. Steps 1--6 apply to the extended proper diagram and give compactified data satisfying (I)--(VI), with $\iota^*=1$.

source.place: §4.1.4(a), final paragraph, and Remark 1.1.3: simultaneous compactification and fixed-diagram restriction

proof.text: For each object take $\rho_Z:Rp_{Z*}u_Z^*\xrightarrow{\sim}u_{\bar Z}^*Rp^*_{Z*}$ to be inverse proper base change [prop-functor-package](4), using the Cartesian squares of Step 7. Its transpose is pullback composition followed by the ordinary counit [fix-prop-adjunctions](4). To check tensor compatibility, transpose along $p_Z^*\dashv Rp_{Z*}$: on both sides the resulting map is the restriction of $\varepsilon_{p_Z^*}\otimes\varepsilon_{p_Z^*}$, by the definition of $t$ in Step 2. For $\alpha_g$, its transpose is the restricted ordinary counit of $p_V^*$; ordinary exchange pasting [fix-lem-exchanges](1),(2) identifies it with the counit defining $\alpha_g$. For $\beta_g$, transpose along $R\bar g_!\dashv\bar g^!$. The two resulting maps are compact-support composition followed by the exceptional counit of $g$. The proper/open normalization [lem-trf-compact-composition-proper-square-normalization](2) identifies compact-support composition across each restriction square with the adjoint of inverse open base change. Exchange composition [fix-lem-exchanges](4) and the composite exceptional counit [fix-prop-adjunctions](3) then identify these two transposes. Use $u^!=u^*$ as specified in [def-trf-cohomological-comparison]. Thus $\rho$ identifies $t,\alpha,\beta$ with the restricted compactified data; at $s$ both maps are the identity. These are exactly the requirements of (VII).

source.place: §4.1.4(a), axiom (VII), with the restriction compatibility of Definition 4.1.2
